_comment: Fragment 116 — curated nodes for D-180 (corrects D-179's three residual defects: B068-R50 AC ownership, R51 target metric/security rows, R52 RACI task-boundary split) and B-069 (D-170 partial-supersession notice, current T5/T6 anchor). Merged 2026-09-02.

nodes.label: D-180: R50-R52 Corrected; D-170 Given a Current Anchor
nodes.description: Chief Editor ruling on B-068 S21's independent re-review of D-179 and B-069's decision-lifecycle finding. Both accepted without dispute, all verified against the actual files before correcting. B068-R50: AC-08a (return/rerun behavior) was attached to FR-05a (independence classification) instead of its actual owner FR-06 -- re-owned. Four target ACs added that existed only as Fn_Spec prose: AC-01a (FR-01, EW start), AC-14a (FR-09, Delivery mutation refusal), AC-16a (FR-10, external-acceptance prerequisite). US-04a/US-05a's dependency chain corrected to stop pointing at historical stories. B068-R51: G-05, SEC-01, SEC-03 only encoded the old human-T5/agent-T6 order with no target counterpart -- added G-05a (evaluated at T6 after bundle reveal, not T5), SEC-01a (T4-to-each-T5-act and each-act-to-T6 separation, target R=A at T6), SEC-03a (target T5 acts are Line 1, T6/T11 stay Line 2). B068-R52: the target RACI matrix modeled two required T5 reviewers as two R holders on one task, contradicting its own one-R-per-task rule -- split into sibling acts T5a (Chief Editorial Desk) and T5b (Chief Journalist), each with exactly one R; the bundle join is now explicit that it is not a task and holds no R or A. Also answers B-069: D-170 is closed but only partially superseded, and a reader landing on it could retrieve obsolete T5/build-status claims with no signal -- added a partial-supersession notice directly above D-170's body classifying each clause current/retained/re-derived/superseded and naming D-180 as the current T5/T6 anchor. D-170's body is unedited and the full target contract is not copied in, avoiding a second drift surface. All new content stays decided_target_held; D-171's S2 hold is unaffected.
nodes.rationale: A decision record that is closed but only partially superseded is a worse navigation trap than one that is wholly current or wholly retired -- a reader has no signal that some clauses still govern and others don't, and the fix is a lifecycle notice at the point of entry rather than a rewrite that would destroy the provenance the record exists to preserve.

nodes.label: B-069: D-170 Needs a Current T5/T6 Anchor
nodes.description: Lane B finding: D-170 is closed as a decision record, but closed does not say which of its clauses remain current. Its body still directly states a single Chief Editorial Desk reviewer at T5 and says the historical T5/T6 order remains build-authorized -- both later superseded by D-171 and D-175. A reader or search result landing on D-170 could retrieve superseded T5 and build-status claims without encountering the correcting decisions, while treating the whole decision as superseded would also be wrong since its F1 axis separation and core F5 A/O/EA authority contract remain valid. Answered by D-180, which adds a partial-supersession notice directly above D-170's body without rewriting it.
nodes.rationale: A decision that is neither wholly current nor wholly superseded needs a lifecycle classification, not a binary status -- collapsing closed/current/build-held/verified into one label is exactly the kind of drift this project's own decision register has caught before under other names.
